Every Budget measure circulating today — the HMRC direct-recovery power, the bank levy, the online marketplace VAT measure, the capital gains decision, the first-time-buyer income caps — is newspaper reporting or briefing, NOT a gov.uk publication. The Treasury's line to the Independent today was a non-confirmation: "decisions on tax are a matter for the chancellor to set out at fiscal events, rather than routinely commenting on rumour, speculation or proposals."

4. A DISCREPANCY TO SETTLE ON THE JACKDAW DATE — NOT A UK COLUMN ITEM, BUT FLAGGING IT.
The gov.uk search API gives "Jackdaw gas field gets green light" a public_timestamp of 2026-10-23T16:30:25Z = 17:30 BST Friday 23 October. This morning's audit file SUN-UK-timestamp-and-staleness-audit.txt states the Jackdaw news release was "published 2026-10-21T06:29:00Z = 07:29 BST Wednesday 21 October 2026". Those are two days apart. One of the two readings is wrong — most likely the morning one read a different field, or the page was first published on the 21st and the search index records a later revision. Do not cite a Jackdaw publication date in tonight's edition without re-opening the page itself.
